deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 41-43). A finite system of pseudo-lines (D_i)_{i in I} in the real projective plane gives a 1-skeleton K. Its vertex set S consists of the crossing points, its edge set A of the segments, and its darts (oriented edges) form the set A-vec. Grothendieck wants to recover the cellular map X (here, the projective plane cut into cells) purely from the combinatorial datum (K, (D_i), omega). By the 'general theorem of maps' this means producing two things. (i) At each vertex s, the pair Z_s of mutually opposite cyclic orders on the darts leaving s. These darts are identified with the oriented pseudo-lines through s. (ii) For each dart a from s to s', a transport bijection psi_a : Z_s -> Z_s' with psi of the reversed dart equal to psi_a^{-1}. This is the usual encoding of maps on possibly non-orientable surfaces: a rotation system up to reversal plus local orientation transport, equivalently a flag/signed rotation system. Such data give a cellular embedding of K in some closed surface X, not necessarily RP^2.

This page states what must be added for the reconstructed X to really carry the D_i as a pseudo-line system in RP^2.

(22) Straight crossing condition. Let nu_s be the number of lines through s, so the vertex has 2 nu_s darts. If rho is the cyclic successor permutation of an order in Z_s, then rho^{nu_s} sends each oriented line through s to its opposite. In other words, the two half-branches of each line are antipodal in the rotation at s, so every line passes straight through each vertex instead of bouncing. The margin note treats nu_s = 2 (degree-4 vertex): then (22) forces the alternating cyclic order and essentially pins rho down.

(23) Euler-Poincaré condition. X = RP^2 is expressed as c0 - c1 + c2 = 1. Here c0 = #S and c1 = #A depend only on K, and c0 - c1 = 1 - c(K), where c(K), the 'degré de connexité', is the cyclomatic number b1(K). So the condition reads c2 = c(K): the number of faces equals the cyclomatic number. Check with 3 lines in general position: V = 3, E = 6, F = 4, b1 = 4. The margin note says that a priori c2 <= c(K), with equality iff X = RP^2. This holds because X is connected and non-orientable (the pseudo-lines are one-sided), so chi(X) <= 1.

(24) Construction of the cyclic orders, begun here. For nu_s >= 3, first build the pair Z'_s of opposite cyclic orders on the set I_s of (unoriented) lines through s. Choose a pseudo-line Delta not through s. The map D_i -> D_i ∩ Delta, from I_s to S_Delta, is injective, since two lines through s already meet at s. S_Delta is cyclically ordered as the vertices of the polygon Delta, so I_s inherits a cyclic order up to reversal. On the next page the axiom (A1) requires this induced order to be independent of Delta. The order is then lifted to the oriented lines (the degree-2 cover from oriented to unoriented lines) compatibly with (22), leaving 2^{nu_s - 1} choices.

The overall programme is an intrinsic, purely combinatorial axiomatization of pseudo-line arrangements: incidence data plus the cyclic orders of crossings along each line, with consistency axioms, from which the cell structure of RP^2 is rebuilt via map theory.
errors: No mathematical errors. The marginal inequality c2 <= c(K) silently needs X connected and non-orientable (true here because pseudo-lines are one-sided closed curves). For an orientable X one would only get c2 <= c(K)+1.
The page is a draft: the construction of Z_s is interrupted (struck-out lines) and the role of the transport bijections psi_a in the RP^2 verification is not yet addressed.

ideas.what: Encoding a cellular embedding in a possibly non-orientable surface by pairs of opposite cyclic orders at vertices plus transport bijections along edges (psi of the reversed dart = psi^{-1}).
ideas.modern_name: Signed / generalized rotation systems; maps as flag systems (Heffter-Edmonds-Ringel for non-orientable surfaces; Tutte)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heffter, Edmonds (1960), Ringel, Tutte; Jones-Singerman (1978) for the algebraic theory of maps
ideas.where_published: Theory of maps / dessins in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) in the oriented setting; non-orientable version unsure

ideas.what: Straight-crossing condition (22): opposite half-branches of each line are antipodal in the rotation at the vertex, i.e. rho^{nu_s} = orientation reversal.
ideas.modern_name: Straight-ahead / 'crossing' condition for pseudo-line arrangements and their maps (central-symmetric local rotation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in the arrangement and oriented-matroid literature (Grünbaum, Goodman-Pollack)

ideas.what: Euler characteristic criterion: the reconstructed surface is RP^2 iff the number of faces equals the cyclomatic number of the 1-skeleton.
ideas.modern_name: Euler's formula for projective arrangements (F = E - V + 1)

ideas.what: Recovering the cyclic order of lines at a vertex s by projecting onto another pseudo-line Delta, with the consistency axiom that the induced cyclic order is independent of Delta.
ideas.modern_name: Local sequences / allowable sequences; rank-3 oriented matroid axioms (chirotopes), Folkman-Lawrence representation

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently develops, around 1981, a map-theoretic (cartes) axiomatization of pseudo-line arrangements. It builds the RP^2 cell structure from incidence data plus cyclic orders of crossings along lines, using rotation systems, straight-crossing and Euler conditions. Mathematically this parallels the Folkman-Lawrence / Goodman-Pollack theory and later local-sequence characterizations. The novelty is historical (Grothendieck's link between his theory of maps/dessins and oriented matroids), not mathematical.
missed.quote: Il faudra ensuite que X soit le plan projectif, ce qui s'exprime par la condition d'EP c_0 - c_1 + c_2 = 1 soit c_2 = c(K)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents Grothendieck's connection between the theory of maps (later dessins d'enfants) and the combinatorics of pseudo-line arrangements / rank-3 oriented matroids. Historians of the Esquisse period may find it relevant; no new theorem appears on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a careful but standard reconstruction of an arrangement's cell structure: rotation systems, straight crossings, Euler characteristic, and projected cyclic orders. All of it is essentially known from oriented matroid / pseudo-line theory. Interest is mainly historical, as Grothendieck's own map-theoretic route.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: '(X, ...)_{i in I}' should read '(D_i)_{i in I}' ('Pour savoir que (D_i)_{i∈I} y forment bien un système de ps. droites').

The symbol in (24) (and in (19) on the previous page) read as 'complement' is Grothendieck's circular-arrow notation for 'set of cyclic orders on'. So Z'_s ⊂ ↺(D_s), i.e. the set of cyclic orders on the set of lines through s, not a complement.
The Euler-Poincaré equation carries the label (23) in the left margin; the transcription omits it.
'X' in 'que X soit le plan projectif' and 'dépend bien sûr de X' is the script 𝒳 (the map/surface).
'Soit ΔD une ps. droite' should read 'Soit Δ ∈ I une ps. droite qui ne passe pas par s'.
'nb de D_i passant par s' refers to nu_s; the clause reads 'si nu_s est le nombre de D_i passant par s, alors rho^{nu_s}(D_i-vec) = (-D_i-vec) pour toute droite orientée D_i-vec passant par s'.
Margin note 3 reads roughly 'NB On a a priori c_2 <= c(K), et (23) équivaut à ...', relating (23) to the face count.
